"""Rounding helpers."""

from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_HALF_UP


def round_half_up(x: float) -> int:
    """Round ``x`` to the nearest integer, ties going away from zero.

    "Half up" here means the common commercial rounding: exact halves are
    rounded away from zero, so 2.5 -> 3 and -2.5 -> -3. Values that are not
    exact ties round to the nearest integer (2.4 -> 2, 2.6 -> 3, -1.2 -> -1).

    The input is converted through ``str`` first so that the decimal value the
    user sees is the one that gets rounded, rather than the binary float
    approximation underneath (e.g. 2.675).
    """
    return int(Decimal(str(x)).quantize(Decimal("1"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP))
EOF
cd /work && python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -20"}

"""Rounding helpers."""

from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_HALF_UP


def round_half_up(x: float) -> int:
    """Round ``x`` to the nearest integer, ties going away from zero.

    "Half up" here means the common commercial rounding: exact halves are
    rounded away from zero, so 2.5 -> 3 and -2.5 -> -3. Values that are not
    exact ties round to the nearest integer (2.4 -> 2, 2.6 -> 3, -1.2 -> -1).

    The input is converted through ``str`` first so that the decimal value the
    user sees is the one that gets rounded, rather than the binary float
    approximation underneath (e.g. 2.675).
    """
    return int(Decimal(str(x)).quantize(Decimal("1"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP))
